name: PT Surya Toto Indonesia Tbk
industry_name: Industrial goods, building products & electrical equipment

frontmatter.title: Surya Toto — a cash-rich sanitary-ware franchise priced for a permanent housing winter
frontmatter.summary: We initiate on PT Surya Toto Indonesia with BUY and a target of Rp277, a total return of 25.6%. The shares discount a permanent collapse in Indonesian housing demand; we see a cyclical trough in FY2026E, a net-cash balance sheet, associates and a bond portfolio worth close to a quarter of the market value marked to earnings, and a captive distribution channel that is both the moat and the main governance risk. Liquidity, not value, is the constraint.
thesis: FY2026E is a cyclical trough, not a structural decline — nine-month sales fell to 1,605.0 from 1,817.5, but the fixed cost base stayed, compressing EBITDA margin to 15.2% from 21.2%; we model recovery from FY2027E with no return to the FY2025 peak before FY2030E.

The balance sheet carries the downside — net cash of -202.6, associates we carry at twelve times their share of FY2025 earnings rather than at their 744.4 book value, a bond portfolio at 149.4, less the unfunded employee-benefit obligation of 384.7 which we deduct in full.
The Toto brand is licensed, not owned — a 1.5% royalty, a 2.5% export commission and 95.8% of sales to related parties are the price of the franchise and the core governance exposure.

Valuation — the FCFF DCF gives Rp362 a share against a price of Rp232; after a 20.0% liquidity discount the target is Rp277. The earnings and EV/EBITDA cross-checks, both on FY2025A metrics, sit -28.8% and -16.0% below the DCF.
A property-cycle turn, cost normalisation and the FY2026 dividend are the catalysts we can date; the free float means the re-rating will be slow.

catalysts.event: FY2026 full-year results and management guidance for the housing cycle
December interim dividend decision, paid in December in each of the last five years
FY2026 final dividend decision under the stated cash-availability policy
Bank Indonesia residential property survey — primary sales and price index
Ceramic and sanitary-ware import protection measures and industry utilisation

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of PT Surya Toto Indonesia with a **BUY** rating and a twelve-month target of Rp277, 25.6% total return including the next dividend. The shares at Rp232 are valued at 6.8x trailing earnings and 0.9x book. The trailing yield on the last final payment alone is 5.6%; the company declared 23 per share for FY2025 in total, interim plus final, which is the number the payout and the income case are built on — a valuation that assumes the current collapse in Indonesian residential construction is permanent rather than cyclical [S2][S4][S7].

The business is a two-segment sanitary-ware and fittings manufacturer. It sells 95.8% of its output to related parties: the Toto Group in Japan, which is also the largest shareholder and the licensor of the brand, and PT Surya Pertiwi Tbk, the listed distribution arm of the same controlling group [S4]. In a normal year this captive channel produces a high-twenties gross margin and a 14.0% return on equity; in a trough year it produces a 15.2% EBITDA margin because the fixed cost base does not move with volume [S2][S4].

Our value rests on three separable blocks. First, the operating franchise: a ten-year FCFF model at a 11.2% WACC gives Rp362 a share, with the terminal value at 56.0% of DCF value. Second, the financial assets net of the financial claims: net cash of -202.6, 149.4 of bonds, and associates we carry at twelve times their share of FY2025 earnings — not at the 744.4 book value, because the pair earned only 759.4 of net assets into a low single-digit return and the 744.4 carrying value is roughly twenty-four times what they earn — less the unfunded employee-benefit obligation of 384.7, which is a claim on equity the cash flow does not charge [S2][S4]. Third, the liquidity penalty: the free float is 7.5% and three-month turnover is IDR126.9m a day. That discount is not our judgement — the house constitution fixes it by turnover band, and at this turnover TOTO falls in the 20.0% band, one band from the harshest — which is why the target sits below our value today of Rp319 [S6].

What would change our mind is not a bad quarter. It is evidence that the related-party channel is being used to transfer value — a step-up in the royalty or commission rates, a change in distributor terms, or a related-party purchase contract priced away from market. None of that is in the accounts today, but it is the risk the discount is for [S4].

PT Surya Toto Indonesia manufactures and sells sanitary ware — closets, basins, urinals, bathtubs and the associated flushing and electronic systems — and the brass and plastic fittings that connect them. The two segments are close to equal in size: sanitary ware contributed 1,152.7 of net sales in FY2025 and fittings 1,099.3, with the small remainder in other products [S4]. The company manufactures in Indonesia and sells both domestically and for export; the FY2025 filing sets out the product lines and the distribution arrangements in the segment and related-party notes [S4].

The commercial architecture is the single most important fact about this company. Sales are made predominantly to related parties — 95.8% of net sales in FY2025 — and within that, the domestic channel runs through PT Surya Pertiwi Tbk, which bought 726.0 of sanitary ware and 906.9 of fittings in FY2025 [S4]. Surya Pertiwi is the listed distributor of the same controlling shareholder group and is the route to market for most Indonesian residential and project demand. The export channel runs to the Toto Group itself: 404.3 of sanitary sales went to group companies abroad in FY2025, up from the prior year, and those sales carry a 2.5% commission payable to Toto Asia Oceania [S4].

The brand is licensed rather than owned. The company pays Toto Limited of Japan a trademark licence fee of 1.5% of net sales on certain products, an arrangement disclosed in the related-party note and charged through operating costs [S4]. In substance this is a franchise: the company gets the TOTO name, the product technology and access to the group's export demand, and pays a royalty plus an export commission for them. That is a defensible commercial arrangement and it is also a permanent leakage of margin that a wholly owned brand would not have.

The shareholder register explains the strategy. Toto Limited of Japan holds 37.9%, PT Multifortuna Asindo 29.4% and PT Suryaparamitra Abadi 24.9%, so the three anchor holders control the company and the free float is 7.5% [S4]. The Japanese parent supplies technology and export demand; the Indonesian holders supply the domestic distribution and the property relationships. Management's stated approach is to defend the premium end of the market and to keep the balance sheet conservative; the FY2025 filing shows no expansion project, no acquisition and no new debt programme [S4].

Operationally the company employed 3,368 people at the last year-end and carried 814.4 of inventory, a level that reflects a deliberate build rather than a stock-out [S4]. The scale is meaningful for Indonesia — the company is the leading domestic sanitary-ware producer — but it is a single-country, single-category manufacturer with one dominant channel, and that concentration frames every number in this report.

Demand for sanitary ware is a derivative of housing completions, not of household formation or GDP directly. Indonesian residential activity has been weak through 2026: Bank Indonesia's residential property survey shows primary-market house sales contracting 8.4% year on year in the third quarter while the residential price index still rose 0.6%, a combination that describes a market clearing on price rather than volume [S7]. Press coverage of the same survey expects the primary market to recover only from 2027 [S8]. Our forecast takes that sequencing seriously: FY2026E revenue falls -7.4% and growth returns in FY2027E at 5.0% [S2][S7].

Supply is fragmented and structurally long. National ceramic plant utilisation ran at 72.0% between January and May 2026, which is an industry producing well below its capacity [S9]. Sanitary ware sits alongside tiles in the same building-materials complex, competing for the same channel shelf space and the same project orders, and weak utilisation tells you that price competition is the default state when demand falls. The government has responded with import controls through the Ministry of Industry, aimed at stemming imported finished goods [S10]; that support helps the domestic producer at the margin but does not create demand.

The competitive set has three parts. Domestic producers compete on brand and on project relationships; TOTO's position in the premium and mid-premium segment is strong because the brand is globally recognised and the product range is complete. Imported product, largely from China, competes on price at the value end and has taken share as household budgets tightened; that is the pressure the import measures are designed to offset [S10]. Adjacent substitutes — plastic cisterns, stainless fixtures, local unbranded ceramics — take the bottom of the market and are not a threat to the premium position.

The moat is real but narrower than it looks. The brand, the licensed technology and the specification into projects are genuine advantages, and the installed base of TOTO product in Indonesian buildings creates a replacement and spare-parts pull. But the distribution that converts that advantage into revenue is a related party, and the customer that buys the exports is the shareholder. A moat that depends on transactions with the controller is a moat with a governance condition attached, and we treat it that way in the valuation rather than as a pure competitive asset [S4].

On the five forces: supplier power is moderate — gas and energy are administered prices, clay and brass are commodities, and imported components carry currency risk — while buyer power is high because one related distributor takes most of the domestic volume. The threat of new entrants is low for premium branded product and high for value ceramics. Rivalry is intense in a down-cycle, as the utilisation figure shows. Substitution is a slow drift rather than a step change [S9][S10].

The Indonesian building-materials chain is structurally cyclical: a long approval and construction lag means that a turn in mortgage demand shows up in ceramic and sanitary-ware orders several quarters later, and a turn in orders shows up in plant utilisation a quarter after that. Manufacturers therefore run their cost base ahead of the cycle and absorb the swing in margin, which is why gross margins in this industry move in wide bands around a stable average.

The external influences that matter for the forecast are the property cycle, the rupiah and energy costs. A weaker rupiah raises the cost of imported components and of the gas-linked inputs, and the company's pricing power in a weak market is limited by the related distributor's own margin needs; that combination is what produced the 22.1% gross margin we model for FY2026E against 26.8% in FY2025 [S2][S4].

The five-year record is a flat top line with a wide margin cycle. Revenue ran 2,086.1 in FY2022 against 2,354.4 in FY2025, a path that never grew faster than the property market; gross margin moved from 27.3% to 26.8% and net profit from 313.4 to 351.2 [S4]. The FY2026E forecast breaks that pattern hard: revenue of 2,180.1, gross margin of 22.1% and net profit of 213.5, an earnings decline of -39.2% at the per-share line [S2].

The nine-month actuals explain the forecast. Sales were 1,605.0 against 1,817.5 in the same period of 2025; gross profit fell to 349.7; operating expenses rose to 178.9, and net profit fell to 152.2 [S2]. The critical asymmetry is that cost of goods sold fell far less than sales. Fixed-asset depreciation of 92.3 and cash employee cost of 707.6 in FY2025 are largely fixed in the short run, so a volume decline is absorbed almost entirely by gross margin — which is exactly what the data pack misses when it uses the cash-flow residual as its depreciation line [S4].

That restatement matters for every margin in this report. The data pack carries a depreciation charge that is a fraction of the true figure because the Indonesian cash-flow statement reports the direct method; the fixed-asset note of the FY2025 filing charges fixed-asset depreciation of 92.3 in FY2025 and 90.4 in FY2024, with right-of-use depreciation of 36.2 on top [S4]. We restate fixed-asset depreciation into the model as facts F7 and F8, treat the lease depreciation as a rent cost that stays inside EBIT, and add the lease liabilities back in the equity bridge so that the lease is not counted twice. Before that restatement the FY2024 margin looks like a collapse; after it, EBITDA margin is 21.2% in FY2025 against 15.2% in FY2026E, which is cyclical compression rather than a structural break [S4].

The revenue build runs through the two segments and the two channels. Domestic sales through Surya Pertiwi carry the housing cycle; exports to the Toto Group carry the Japanese parent's own sourcing decisions, which have been a modest tailwind — group export sales of 404.3 in FY2025 were higher than the year before [S4]. We model no share gain in either channel: domestic volume follows the property survey, exports grow with group demand at the long-run rate, and neither segment is assumed to recover its FY2025 peak before the end of the decade. Fittings recovered faster than sanitary ware in FY2025 and we expect the same ordering in the recovery, because fittings are specified later in the construction cycle [S4].

Costs are the swing factor. Cash paid to employees was 707.6 in FY2025 and the nine-month 2026 expense line grew even as sales fell, which is the signature of a company defending its capability rather than cutting into the recovery [S2][S4]. We hold opex at 11.0% of sales in FY2026E, easing to 10.6% by FY2030E only as revenue spreads over the base. Capex was 83.0 in FY2025 and we model 5.5% of sales in FY2026E, falling to 4.0% thereafter, in line with maintenance depreciation; no expansion project is disclosed in the filings, so no growth capex is assumed [S2][S4].

Working capital is the reason FY2026E free cash flow is negative. Operating working capital was 941.4 at the last year-end and we set FY2026E at the 30 September 2026 actual of 1,122.8, absorbing 181.4 of build rather than assuming a fourth-quarter release [S2][S4]. Inventories were 814.4 at end-2025 and higher again in September; the company has kept producing into a falling market, which is defensible for a fixed-cost plant but expensive in cash. Alongside it, trade receivables from related parties rose to 503.2 at 30 September 2026 from 457.4 at end-2025 while revenue fell -7.4%: the related distributor is taking longer to pay, not less. Nearly nine-tenths of that balance is one counterparty — 451.6 due from PT Surya Pertiwi against 397.9 at the prior year-end [S2]. The expected-credit-loss allowance for the whole book was 2.5 at end-2025, which is a provisioning model that covers the ageing bucket beyond six months and nothing younger: a receivable that is slow rather than impaired still carries at face. With capex of 119.0 against 83.0 in FY2025, free cash flow to the firm falls to -22.7 in FY2026E from 278.0, then recovers to 205.4 as the working-capital drag stops and margins rebuild [S2][S4].

The balance sheet is the strongest part of the case and it is why a negative cash-flow year does not threaten the dividend. Equity was 2,568.5 at end-2025 and book value per share 248.9; the company ended FY2025 in net cash of -202.6 [S4]. The 30 September 2026 position is what the forecast is anchored on: cash of 266.1, short-term bank borrowings of 5.0, a current portion of long-term borrowings of 17.5 and long-term borrowings of 61.1, plus lease liabilities of 41.5 short and 107.1 long [S2]. Our FY2026E close is net cash of -70.6 on debt of 232.1 and cash of 302.7: the fourth quarter adds operating cash and pays the December interim dividend, which the company has declared and paid in December in every year on the record [S6]. The reconciliation is deliberately tight — we do not model a Q4 working-capital release that the nine-month accounts do not show — and it still leaves the dividend covered from the balance sheet if the cycle takes another year to turn. The DCF is struck on the September net debt because that is the valuation date; the FY2026E closing figure is the model's own cash path, used for interest and for the year-end leverage picture, not for the bridge.

Two off-income-statement claims sit against that cash. The unfunded long-term employee-benefit obligation was 384.7 at 30 September 2026 (387.8 at end-2025), roughly ninety-seven per cent unfunded, and we now deduct it in full in the equity bridge rather than disclosing it: FCFF charges only the annual service and interest cost, not the obligation itself, so a buyer of the equity inherits it [S2][S4]. The lease liabilities of 41.5 and 107.1 are treated the other way — the rent is charged inside EBIT through right-of-use depreciation, so the liabilities are added back to equity value to avoid counting the lease twice [S2]. Associates of 744.4 and bonds of 149.4 are carried at cost on the same balance sheet; both are valued separately below, and neither at book.

Capital allocation is simple and shareholder-friendly within the constraint of the group structure. Dividends paid were 216.8 in FY2025 and the declared FY2025 dividend was 23 per share, on a stated policy of paying out cash available after capex rather than a fixed ratio [S4][S6]. Our payout assumption is 67.6%, the ratio implied by the FY2025 declaration, held flat. One caution on the model's history: the dividend line in the engine carries the final payment of 13.0 per share rather than the declared total for the year, so we read the payout, the yield and the income case off the declaration schedule, not off the model's dividend history [S4][S6].

Earnings quality, screened on the house card. Cash conversion is where the trough shows up before the margin does. Net profit stays positive at 213.5 in FY2026E while free cash flow to the firm is -22.7, and the whole of that gap is working capital and capex taken at the nine-month run-rate, not capitalised cost, a receivable-timing gain or a revaluation [S2]. Across the cycle the accrual position has been benign — the FY2025 cash flow funded 216.8 of dividends and 83.0 of capex and still added to cash — so we do not read the current year as earnings outrunning cash; we read it as the cycle taking its working capital back [S4]. The receivables build is the line to watch: the allowance covers only the ageing bucket beyond six months, so an impairment, if it came, would arrive as a step rather than a trend, and the bear case is built with a further working-capital build rather than a release. Related-party flows are the dominant structural flag: 95.8% of revenue, 85.2 of purchases from an affiliate of a shareholder, and a licence and commission arrangement with the parent [S4]. This is disclosed, audited and priced, so we classify it as an optics-class structure flag rather than a manipulation-class one — but it is the flag that would become fatal if the terms moved. On the exchange side we found no special-monitoring-board designation, no special notation and no going-concern or late-filing disclosure in the archived filings; the risk here is structure and liquidity, not reporting integrity. The FY2025 accounts carry an unmodified opinion from KAP Purwanto Susanti dan Surja, a member firm of Ernst & Young, with revenue recognition on related-party sales as a key audit matter and confirmation letters sent to the related parties [S4].

A capital-intensive, single-country manufacturer with a stable margin band, maintenance-level capex and a visible cash payout is the natural case for a discounted cash flow as the primary method. We weight FCFF DCF at 60%, the earnings multiple at 20%, EV/EBITDA at 10% and dividend yield at 10% — a deliberate tilt away from the template default, because FY2026E is a trough year and a multiple applied to trough earnings says more about the cycle than about value. We are explicit about what the two earnings cross-checks actually use: both are computed on FY2025A, the last audited year, not on our FY2026E trough. On FY2026E earnings the same peer median would give a materially lower number, so the cross-checks as presented flatter the DCF rather than support it, and the reader should treat them as an upper bound on what the multiples can defend [S2][S6].

The cost of capital is built bottom-up in rupiah. The risk-free rate is 7.4% — the Indonesian government curve at the long end — plus a mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2% and a country risk premium of 2.5%. The industry unlevered beta is 0.80, relevered at a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.10 to 0.86, giving a cost of equity of 11.6%. Pre-tax cost of debt is 9.4% — consistent with the 16.6 finance cost on the opening debt in FY2025 — and at a 8.8% debt weight the WACC is 11.2%, at the bottom of the house range for Indonesian equities and justified by the net-cash balance sheet [S4].

The DCF runs ten explicit years to FY2035E, which is long enough for the property cycle to turn and for margins to normalise without assuming a return to the FY2025 peak: gross margin reaches 25.8% by FY2030E, still below the five-year best, and terminal growth is 4.5% nominal — below long-run Indonesian nominal GDP and consistent with a housing-linked volume driver [S7]. The result is Rp362 per share from an enterprise value of 3,419.1, with the terminal value at 56.0% of DCF value. That terminal share is on the high side of comfortable, and we test it explicitly rather than wave it through.

The multiple-survival test. Capitalising the terminal value against FY2035E EBITDA of 616.4 implies an exit EV/EBITDA above the 7.0x the market pays on our trough year and far above the 4.4x it pays on FY2025A. We will not dress that up: the DCF needs the multiple to expand, and that expansion is the weakest link in the valuation. What keeps it defensible is that the FY2035E margin of 19.1% is still below the FY2025 actual of 21.2%, so the terminal value is not paying for margin expansion beyond the last cycle — it pays for a normalised cycle plus growth — and that the business at that point carries a decade of cash generation, a net-cash balance sheet and no refinancing need, whereas today's multiple is struck in a trough month on a sector the market prices for distress. The 5.7 peer median the cross-check uses comes from that same distressed month and is a floor, not a fair multiple. A reader who refuses the expansion should haircut the DCF by its cost; with the terminal value at 56.0% of DCF value, that haircut is material, and it is the main reason our target sits below the DCF value.

The equity bridge starts from enterprise value and settles the non-operating items at the 30 September 2026 balance sheet. We add the 149.4 bond portfolio at carrying value, and add back the lease liabilities of 41.5 and 107.1 because the rent is already charged inside EBIT through right-of-use depreciation. We deduct the 384.7 employee-benefit obligation in full: FCFF charges the annual service cost, not the obligation, so a buyer of the equity inherits an unfunded promise of that size. And we mark the associates down rather than up. The two stakes carry at 744.4, but one is an office building that earned 48.6 in FY2025 and the other a sanitary manufacturer that earned 14.1 — a combined return on their own net assets well below the cost of equity — so we capitalise our share of their FY2025 profit at twelve times. Twelve times is generous against a 11.6% cost of equity, and it is the benchmark the red team proposed; at our cost of equity a business earning a mid single-digit return on equity is worth a discount to that multiple, not a premium. There is no minority interest to deduct. The result is Rp362 per share.

The cross-checks diverge in a way that is diagnostic, and they are quoted on FY2025A metrics throughout. The P/E cross-check gives Rp258, -28.8% against the DCF, applying the 7.6 peer median to FY2025A net profit of 351.2 rather than to our trough earnings. That is the higher of the two possible anchors: on the FY2026E trough the same multiple would give a materially lower number, and a cross-check that capitalises the trough twice tells us nothing about value. Even on the higher base it sits below the DCF, which is the honest reading — at the multiple the market pays for comparable Indonesian manufacturers, the last audited earnings support less than our cash flow model. The EV/EBITDA cross-check gives Rp305, -16.0%, applying the same peer median of 5.7 to FY2025A EBITDA of 499.2, with the associates and bonds already netted in the multiple. The dividend-yield method gives Rp194, -46.5%, on the next twelve months' distribution of Rp14 per share against a required yield of 7.2%; a payout calibrated to trough cash flow produces a low distribution, and a low floor in a trough year is what a floor should look like [S0][S4].

The cross-check the engine does not run. Price-to-book is the natural lens for a manufacturer whose value is its asset base, and the house template does not allow it as a weighted method for a corporate, so we use it as a test rather than a value. At the price the shares trade at 0.9x book, against a cost of equity of 11.6% and terminal growth of 4.5%. A justified multiple of return on equity less growth over cost of equity less growth sits above book when fed the FY2025A return of 14.0%, and below book when fed the FY2027E recovery return of 9.1%. The two bracket our DCF, which is the right way to read it: the valuation is a bet on how much of the FY2025 return is recoverable, not on the size of the asset base — and the asset base is what protects the downside.

Sensitivity is dominated by gross margin and the discount rate, not by terminal growth. A one-point move in the long-run gross margin is worth more than a full point of terminal growth, because the margin determines the cash flow that the terminal value capitalises. That is why the assumptions file spends its sourced justification on margin recovery and leaves terminal growth at a conservative 4.5% [S2][S7].

What the price implies. At Rp232 the shares trade at 6.8x of FY2025A earnings, 11.2x of our trough FY2026E earnings and 9.7x of the recovery year, with an EV/EBITDA of 4.4x on FY2025A and 7.0x on the trough — and those multiples already net the bond portfolio and the associates, because the engine deducts investments from enterprise value. The market is therefore paying below the 5.7 peer median on the last audited EBITDA and below the 7.6 peer median on the last audited earnings. A reverse solve in our engine does not bracket the price with a single growth assumption, so we do not quote one; the direct reading is enough. To justify Rp232 on our own FY2026E cash flow you need either a cost of capital several points above the 11.2% we use or a terminal growth rate that has the business shrinking in real terms — and both of those describe a company in run-off, which is not what the FY2025 accounts, the balance sheet or the dividend record show [S4][S6]. The gap between the price and our Rp319 value today is the opportunity; the 20.0% discount we apply to reach the Rp277 target is the price of being able to own it.

The largest risk is the related-party channel, and it is a risk of terms rather than of demand. The distributor that takes most of the domestic volume is controlled by the same shareholders as the company; the licensor is the largest shareholder; the export customer is the parent. A change in transfer pricing — a higher royalty, a higher export commission, different distributor discounts — would move value from minority holders to the group without ever showing up as a bad quarter [S4]. Likelihood is low in any single year and impact is high, because the entire margin structure runs through those contracts. Mitigation is disclosure: the arrangements are in the audited related-party note and are approved as such, and the auditor's key audit matter is precisely revenue recognition on those sales [S4].

The second risk is the cycle running longer than we model. Our base case already assumes FY2026E revenue falls -7.4% and margins recover only gradually; a property market that stays in contraction through 2027 would take revenue another leg down against a fixed cost base, and the bear case is built on exactly that [S7][S8]. The third is import competition: if protection is diluted or the rupiah strengthens, imported product competes harder at the value end and the domestic producer defends share with price [S10]. The fourth is input cost and currency — gas, energy and imported components — where a weaker rupiah hits cost with a lag and pricing power is constrained [S2].

The fifth is the receivable. Nearly nine-tenths of the trade book is owed by the related distributor, it grew while sales fell, and the allowance provides only for what is already more than six months past due [S2]. If the distributor's own cash conversion deteriorates further, Surya Toto either extends more credit or books an impairment; the first is a working-capital drag, the second a hit to book value and to the dividend. This is a related-party risk with a number attached rather than a disclosure risk, and it is why we do not model a working-capital release in the base case.

The sixth is liquidity, index mechanics and supply. The free float is 7.5% on the pack's measure — the register arithmetic gives 37.9% held by Toto Limited, 29.4% by PT Multifortuna Asindo and 24.9% by PT Suryaparamitra Abadi, leaving a stub — and three-month turnover is IDR126.9m a day [S4]. The exchange raised the minimum free float for continued listing to 15.0% in 2026; issuers below a market capitalisation of Rp5.0 trillion have until 31 March 2029 to comply, and TOTO, valued well below that threshold at the current price, is in the later bucket, so this is a dated obligation rather than a live threat [S11]. Compliance can be met by the controlling holders selling down or by issuing new shares, and the second dilutes per-share value at a price near book; either way the float is too thin to absorb supply, which is what the 20.0% discount is for. The stock also fails our own investability screen on turnover even though it passes on size and board. The seventh is the unfunded employee-benefit obligation of 384.7, which is a genuine claim on equity and now sits in the bridge as a deduction, not a footnote [S2].

The scenarios are mirrored on the same three drivers. The bear case shocks revenue growth down by three points, gross margin down by one and a half points and working capital up by four points of sales; the bull case moves each by the same amount the other way, and probabilities put half the weight on the base because it is the most probable path rather than the mid-point of our doubts [S2][S7]. The balance-sheet items do not vary by scenario: the bond portfolio, the lease add-back, the employee-benefit deduction and the associate mark are carried at probability one in all three, so no scenario gets a second helping of asset value. The bull case earns its balance-sheet leg through the working-capital shock instead — a release rather than a build, which is the cash-flow expression of the same recovery — and it requires the housing turn a year early with operating leverage on the fixed base, which the FY2025 accounts show the business can deliver when volume returns [S4]. The bear value of Rp295 is still above the current price, which is the point: the downside is protected by assets and by a trough multiple, not by our forecast.

Signposts that would change the view: two consecutive quarters of positive year-on-year primary housing sales in the Bank Indonesia survey; gross margin recovering above 23.6% with revenue growth; receivables and inventory falling in absolute terms; a dividend declared at or above the prior year, including the December interim; any change to the royalty, commission or distributor terms; and any announcement on the free float ahead of the 31 March 2029 deadline [S7][S6][S4][S11].

Control is concentrated and the structure is the story. Toto Limited of Japan holds 37.9%, PT Multifortuna Asindo 29.4% and PT Suryaparamitra Abadi 24.9%, and the three together account for all but a stub of the register [S4]. The pack puts the free float at 7.5%; the arithmetic from those three holdings is consistent with a float of that order, and we use the pack figure in the valuation because it is the one the liquidity screen consumes. The exchange raised the minimum free float for continued listing to 15.0% in 2026, with a 31 March 2029 deadline for issuers below a market capitalisation of Rp5.0 trillion — TOTO's category — so the company has a dated obligation to widen the float, by sell-down or by new shares, and the second route would dilute at a price near book [S11]. There is no dual-class structure and no rights issue in the recent record: the share count has been unchanged, and the listing history page shows no corporate action that would dilute per-share value [S6]. We found no pledge of the anchor holders' shares in the archived filings; that is a statement about what is disclosed, and a reader should treat a future pledge disclosure as a material negative because the float is too thin to absorb margin-driven supply [S4].

Related-party dealings are extensive, quantified and the central governance fact. Sales to related parties were 95.8% of revenue in FY2025 [S4]. Purchases of work-in-process fittings from PT Dian Surya Global, a company owned by one of the shareholders, were 85.2, and the company also rents buildings from group entities [S4]. The royalty is 1.5% of net sales on certain products and the export commission is 2.5% [S4]. None of this is hidden; all of it is in the audited note and approved as a related-party transaction. The question for a minority holder is not disclosure but terms, and the only protection is the audit committee and the independent shareholders' approval process.

The audit is clean and the auditor is a major firm. KAP Purwanto Susanti dan Surja, a member firm of Ernst & Young, issued an unmodified opinion on the FY2025 accounts, with revenue recognition on related-party sales as a key audit matter and confirmation procedures with the related parties described in the report [S4]. The dividend record is consistent rather than progressive: 23 per share was declared for FY2025, inside the range declared over the last four years, and the payout of 67.6% of earnings follows a policy tied to cash after capex rather than a fixed ratio [S4][S6]. The board is the standard two-tier Indonesian structure of commissioners and directors; the filings disclose remuneration in aggregate, and we note that the controlling shareholders sit on both sides of the related-party contracts [S4].

On ESG, the material exposures are energy and water intensity in ceramics firing, labour practices in manufacturing, and product-level water efficiency, where the premium end of the market is being pushed toward lower-flush product. The company reports no environmental controversy in the archived set and no enforcement action; we do not treat ESG as a valuation driver here, but the energy intensity is a cost exposure as much as an environmental one, which is why gas prices sit in our margin assumptions [S4][S9].

The dated catalysts are the FY2026 results in February 2027, when management will guide on the property cycle and the FY2027 cost base; the December interim dividend decision, which the company has taken in November and paid in December in each of the last five years, and the FY2026 final dividend decision in mid-2027 under the stated cash-availability policy; the quarterly Bank Indonesia residential property survey, which is the single best high-frequency read on the demand driver; and the 31 March 2029 free-float deadline, with anything announced sooner on a sell-down or share issuance a live catalyst in both directions [S2][S6][S7][S11]. On the supply side, the ceramic industry utilisation data and any change in import protection are the events that would move the competitive backdrop [S9][S10].

The KPIs we monitor between updates: nine-month and full-year revenue against the property survey; gross margin, which is the operating-leverage read; inventory in absolute terms and as days of sales; receivables against revenue and the ageing of the related-party balance, which is where an impairment would appear first; operating cash flow against net profit; the related-party sales percentage and the royalty and commission rates; the declared dividend, interim and final; and turnover, because a float this thin can re-rate on very little flow [S2][S4][S6].

bear.narrative: Property completions stay depressed through 2027 and the rupiah stays weak, so the related-party distributor cannot absorb higher prices; volume falls, the fixed cost base stays, and gross margin stays near the 2026 trough with inventory liquidated at a discount.

bull.narrative: Housing recovery arrives a year early, exports to the Toto Group grow, and the rupiah stabilises so imported material costs stop rising; operating leverage on a fixed cost base takes gross margin back toward the FY2025 peak with working capital released.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E -7.4% follows the nine-month actual (nine-month sales Rp1,605.0bn against Rp1,817.5bn in nine months 2025) plus a Q4 at the Q3 run-rate; FY2027E +5.0% and FY2028E +5.5% assume the residential property cycle bottoms in 2026 and recovers from 2027 (BI survey shows primary house sales contracting 8.43% yoy in Q3 2026 while prices still rise 0.58%) [S2, S7, S8], with volumes recovering against a fixed cost base; FY2029-30E fade to 4.5% and 4.0%. Base does not assume a return to the FY2025 sales peak before FY2030.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 22.1% is the nine-month actual (gross profit Rp349.7bn on sales Rp1,605.0bn, a 4.3pp fall) carried into Q4 at the Q3 rate; COGS fell only 6.5% against an 11.7% sales fall, so the fixed conversion cost base (fixed-asset depreciation Rp92.3bn, employee cash cost Rp707.6bn) was spread over less volume [S2, S4]. From FY2027E margins recover with volume to the FY2022-25 average of 25.8% by FY2030E (22.1% to 25.8% by FY2035E flat thereafter): the four-year record is 27.3%, 24.0%, 25.0% and 26.8%, so the recovery target is the average, not the peak, and the evidence for a permanently lower band (import competition, 72% industry utilisation) describes a cyclical trough rather than a new margin floor [S4, S9, S10].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 11.0% is the nine-month actual (operating expenses Rp178.9bn on Rp1,605.0bn): the expense base is largely fixed staff cost and lease depreciation and did not fall with sales [S2]. It eases to 10.6% by FY2030E only as revenue recovers over a cost base growing ~4% a year; it never returns to the FY2025 9.5% because we do not assume the FY2025 volume peak.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Fixed-asset depreciation only, Rp92.3bn in FY2025 on sales of Rp2,354.4bn [S4]. Right-of-use depreciation (Rp36.2bn) is a lease cost that stays inside EBIT and is not added back here, so the lease liability is excluded from net debt through the valuation bridge.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Nine-month 2026 capex was Rp87.6bn (fixed-asset purchases Rp80.3bn plus down payments of Rp7.3bn, Q1 15.5 + Q2 28.0 + Q3 44.1) on sales of Rp1,605.0bn, i.e. 5.46%, so FY2026E is set at that run-rate rather than the earlier 4.8% [S2]. It falls to 3.9-4.0% from FY2027E, in line with fixed-asset depreciation at maintenance level. No new plant or expansion project is announced in the filings, so no growth capex is assumed.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is set at the 30 September 2026 actual: operating working capital Rp1,122.1bn on a full-year revenue base, i.e. 51.5% of sales, so no fourth-quarter release is assumed against a third-quarter build of Rp180.7bn (trade receivables Rp503.2bn and inventories Rp887.4bn at 30 September against Rp457.4bn and Rp814.4bn at end-2025) [S2, S4]. The ratio eases from FY2027E as volume recovers and the inventory and receivable build normalises, reaching 47% by FY2030E — still above the 40.0% FY2025 actual.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Nine months 2026 tax of Rp42.9bn on pre-tax profit of Rp195.1bn is 22.0%; FY2025 was 20.0% after adjustments [S2, S4].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance cost Rp16.6bn on opening total debt of Rp204.6bn (bank borrowings plus lease liabilities) = 8.1% [S4].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance income Rp20.4bn on opening cash of Rp335.7bn, plus the Rp149.4bn bond holding [S4]; 5.5% is set on cash only, below the FY2025 realised yield, because rates on IDR deposits have fallen and the bond is valued separately in the bridge.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Debt is small and stable but did move in the nine months: total debt of Rp232.1bn at 30 September 2026 (bank borrowings Rp83.5bn plus lease liabilities Rp148.5bn) against Rp204.6bn at end-2025, so FY2026E carries the actual Rp27.5bn increase and no further borrowing is assumed thereafter [S2, S4].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Share of net profit of the two associates (Rp31.2bn in FY2025, Rp19.1bn in nine months 2026), which sits below EBIT and is therefore outside FCFF; the stakes are valued separately in the equity bridge at twelve times our share of their profit, not at book [S4, S2].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: No minority interests on the balance sheet [S4].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 dividends paid Rp216.8bn and the FY2025 declared dividend was Rp23 per share (Rp10 interim plus Rp13 final) on EPS of Rp34 = 67.6%; declarations have ranged between Rp18 and Rp24 per share over the last four fiscal years, so the ratio is set by cash availability after capex rather than by a fixed policy [S4, S6]. 67.6% is held through the forecast.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: 10,320,000,000 shares issued and paid up, unchanged since the 2016 split; no corporate action announced [S6, S4].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 4.5% nominal, below long-run Indonesian nominal GDP (real growth plus the 3.28% CPI of the same Bank Indonesia survey) and equal to the FY2030E revenue growth we model: a sanitary-ware maker whose volumes are tied to housing completions should not be assumed to shrink in real terms for ever, and 4.5% is inside the house cap for rupiah terminal growth [S7].

challenges.challenge: The bridge adds the Rp744.4bn associates at book and calls it a conservative choice because a market multiple on their earnings would be higher than book. The associates earned Rp31.2bn in FY2025 and Rp19.1bn in 9M2026, so book is 24x trailing (29x annualised) earnings and a 4.2% ROE on their own net assets; a market or earnings multiple would put them well below book, not above. At 12x earnings the stake is worth c.Rp372bn, cutting c.Rp36/share from the target.
challenges.answer: Associates are now marked in the bridge from book to twelve times our share of FY2025 profit (Rp31.2bn), a Rp370.5bn markdown; book is c.24x earnings on a 4.2% return on their own net assets, not conservative, and 12x is still generous against an 11.6% cost of equity and a 7.6x peer median [S4].

challenges.challenge: The EV-to-equity bridge omits the long-term employee-benefit liability of Rp384.7bn at 30 Sep 2026 (DBO Rp392.8bn less only Rp12.0bn of plan assets at end-2025, i.e. c.97% unfunded). It is a balance-sheet claim on equity, not an operating cost, and at Rp37.3/share is 12% of the target. The report both acknowledges a conservative reader should deduct it and then does not deduct it.
challenges.answer: The Rp384.7bn long-term employee-benefit obligation at 30 September 2026 is now deducted in full in the equity bridge, and section 3 explains that FCFF charges only the annual service cost, so the unfunded balance is a claim on equity a buyer inherits [S2].

challenges.challenge: The bridge adds back FY2025 lease liabilities of Rp38.8bn and Rp138.6bn (F31/F32) while net debt of -33.9 is computed from the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet, whose total lease liability is Rp148.5bn (Rp41.5bn current plus Rp107.1bn non-current). The Rp28.8bn difference overstates equity by Rp2.8/share.
challenges.answer: The lease add-backs now use the 30 September 2026 balances (Rp41.5bn current, Rp107.1bn non-current) so they match the date of the net-debt figure; the FY2025 balances are no longer used [S2].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the P/E cross-check applies a normal multiple of 7.6 to trough earnings of 20.7 per share and that EV/EBITDA capitalises the same trough EBITDA the DCF does. The engine applies both to FY2025A: P/E on NP of Rp351.2bn (EPS 34.03) gives Rp258, and EV/EBITDA on Rp499.2bn gives Rp381. On the actual trough metrics they would be c.Rp157 and c.Rp288, so the within-tolerance agreement with the DCF disappears.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states that both earnings cross-checks are computed on FY2025A metrics (P/E on net profit of Rp351.2bn, EV/EBITDA on EBITDA of Rp499.2bn) and says plainly that on the FY2026E trough the same peer medians would give materially lower values, so the multiples are an upper bound, not confirmation [S0, S4].

challenges.challenge: The summary's trailing dividend yield of 5.6% is the final payment only (Rp13/232). The engine's own market block carries dps_ttm of Rp23, and sections 3 and 6 state Rp23 was declared for FY2025 (S2 shows the Rp13 final of Rp134.16bn paid in 2026 plus the Rp10 interim). The trailing/forward cash yield is therefore c.9.9%, not 5.6% - the income case is understated by 4.3pp.
challenges.answer: The 5.6% yield is now labelled explicitly as the last final payment alone, and the declared FY2025 total of Rp23 per share (Rp10 interim plus Rp13 final) is given from the engine market block and the company dividend record [S6].

challenges.challenge: Section 3 says the FY2026 cash-flow gap is working capital - inventory - not a receivable or capitalisation effect. Trade receivables rose to Rp503.2bn at 30 Sep 2026 from Rp457.4bn at end-2025 (+10%) while 9M revenue fell 11.7%, and 87% of FY2025 receivables (Rp397.9bn of Rp457.4bn) were due from related distributor PT Surya Pertiwi; DSO rose from c.71 to c.85 days. That is the related-party credit / channel risk the thesis itself calls fatal, and it is absent from the bear case.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now quantifies the receivables build (Rp503.2bn against Rp457.4bn), names PT Surya Pertiwi at Rp451.6bn against Rp397.9bn, and shows the allowance of Rp2.5bn covers only the over-six-month bucket; the bear case already carries a further working-capital build [S2, S4].

challenges.challenge: The model's FY2026E cash of Rp387.7bn and net debt of -183.1 do not reconcile to the 30 Sep 2026 actuals of Rp266.1bn cash and -33.9 net debt. With 9M operating cash flow of only Rp34.8bn against Rp152.2bn of net profit, the model's FY2026 delta-NWC of Rp83.3bn is below the actual 9M build, so it implicitly books a c.Rp100bn Q4 working-capital release while section 3 says no release is assumed.
challenges.answer: FY2026E is calibrated to the nine-month actuals: working capital at 51.5% of sales (delta Rp181.4bn against the Rp180.7bn actual build, no Q4 release), capex at 5.46%, closing cash of Rp302.7bn and net debt of -Rp70.6bn; the DCF bridge uses the 30 September net debt of -Rp33.9bn because that is the valuation date [S2].

challenges.challenge: A 20% liquidity discount (Rp78/share, 25% of the Rp311 target, larger than the entire Rp44 bear-versus-base spread) is asserted as the house liquidity discount with no cited house rule. A thin 7.76% float supports a discount, not necessarily its size; at 10% the target would be c.Rp349 and at 15% c.Rp330.
challenges.answer: The summary now states that the discount is fixed mechanically by the house constitution's turnover band, not judged, and names the applicable band at the three-month turnover of Rp126.9m a day, one band from the harshest; the undiscounted value and DCF value remain in section 4 as the reference without it [S6].

challenges.challenge: The base caps gross margin at 25.5% in perpetuity, 1.3pp below the FY2022-25 average (25.8%) and 1.3pp below FY2025 (26.8%), and uses terminal growth of 4.0% against c.8.6% nominal GDP (real 5.29% plus CPI 3.28%). The sourced evidence (import competition, 72% utilisation) explains a cyclical trough, not a permanently lower margin, and Q3 2026 gross margin already recovered to 23.2% from 21.0% in H1.
challenges.answer: Gross margin now recovers to the FY2022-25 average of 25.8% by FY2030E and is held there, and terminal growth is 4.5%, inside the 5% rupiah cap; the drift justification was rewritten to match [S4, S7].

challenges.challenge: The stock trades at 0.93x book with a 14% normal-year ROE; at the report's own COE of 11.6% and g of 4.0% the justified P/B is (0.14-0.04)/(0.116-0.04) = 1.32x = c.Rp328, an independent cross-check above the Rp311 target. The engine can compute this but the blend uses only DCF, P/E, EV/EBITDA and dividend yield, so the most natural bull anchor for an asset-backed compounder is absent.
challenges.answer: A P/B-ROE cross-check is added in section 4 using the stock's 0.93x book, the 11.6% cost of equity and 4.5% growth: on FY2025A ROE it sits above book and on the FY2027E recovery ROE below, bracketing the DCF; it is not blended because the corporate template does not permit it [S4].

challenges.challenge: The bull case monetises none of the identifiable balance-sheet upside: associates (744.4), bonds (149.4) and net cash (33.9) are Rp90/share, 39% of the price, so the operating franchise trades at only c.4.4x FY2026E EBITDA after deducting them, and the Rp73bn inventory / Rp46bn receivable build the report calls upside is never booked in any scenario.
challenges.answer: The bridge items are carried at probability one in all three scenarios, so the bull cannot take the assets twice; its balance-sheet leg is the mirrored working-capital shock (-4pp of sales), which is the cash-flow form of the inventory and receivable release. No sourced bull asset uplift exists, so none is booked [S4, S2].

challenges.challenge: Section 6 says the 7.5% float is far below the exchange's free-float minimum but cites S6, a listing chronology that contains no free-float rule, and never states the 15% minimum, its March-2027 deadline or the consequence (index exclusion or a dilutive placement). For a stock priced on a 7.76% float, a forced float increase is a supply event, and the register arithmetic is 92.24% held / 7.76% free, not 91.2% / 7.5%.
challenges.answer: Section 6 now cites the exchange rule to S11: a 15% minimum for continued listing, with issuers below Rp5tn of market capitalisation given until 31 March 2029, so TOTO's deadline is 2029 not 2027; the register arithmetic (92.24% held, 7.76% free) is acknowledged and the source is corrected [S11, S4].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E capex is set at 4.8% of sales (Rp104.7bn) although 9M capex was Rp87.6bn on Rp1,605.0bn of sales, i.e. 5.46%, and Q4 would need only Rp17.1bn to reach the model - understating capex by c.Rp13bn (Rp1.3/share). Section 5 also gives turnover as IDR126.9m million rupiah a day where the market block has Rp126.9m/day.
challenges.answer: FY2026E capex is set at the nine-month run-rate of 5.46% of sales (Rp87.6bn on Rp1,605.0bn, including down payments), and the liquidity sentence now reads turnover in rupiah a day with the duplicate unit removed [S2, S6].

missing_bull_case.note: The justified P/B-ROE cross-check (14% normal ROE, COE 11.6%, g 4.0% gives 1.32x book = Rp328) is absent from the method blend, and the Rp90/share non-operating asset backstop plus the 73bn inventory / 46bn receivable build the report calls upside are never monetised in the base or bull. Bull 445 is only the mirror of the bear (+16%).

missing_bear_case.note: Receivables rose to 503.2bn at 30 Sep 2026 from 457.4bn (+10%) while 9M revenue fell 11.7%, with 87% due from the related distributor PT Surya Pertiwi and DSO up c.14 days; the report explicitly says the cash gap is not a receivable. The 7.76% free float against the 15% IDX minimum is flagged but uncited and unquantified.

assumption_realism.note: The operating build is sound and reconciles to the interim figures (Q4 575.1 = Q3 574.9; FY gross margin 22.1% = 9M 21.8% plus Q4 at Q3 23.2%). But FY2026E capex of 4.8% of sales is below the 5.46% 9M run-rate, and the associates earn only 4.2% on book.

evidence_and_citations.note: Revenue, 9M gross profit/NP, associates, bonds, benefit liability, royalty, shareholders, BI survey and the auditor/KAM were all verified in S2/S3/S4/S7. But the 5.6% trailing yield ignores the Rp23 declared, section 6's 91.2%/7.5% float should be 92.24%/7.76%, the free-float rule is cited to S6 which does not contain it, and the P/E and EV/EBITDA cross-check metrics are misdescribed.

valuation_method_fit.note: FCFF DCF is the right primary method and the multiple-survival test is run properly. The bridge, however, omits the Rp384.7bn long-term employee-benefit liability (only 12.0bn of plan assets against a 392.8bn DBO), values the 744.4bn associates at book while calling it conservative (book is 24x their 31.2bn share of profit), and adds back FY2025 lease balances of 177.4 against a 9M2026 net debt that contains only 148.5.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose leans on downside protection by assets while the bear (340) is only 11.5% below base and 47% above the price, and the income case is understated at 5.6%. Still, the conclusion survives the bear probability doubled (c.Rp302, +30%), so the bias is presentational rather than thesis-breaking.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: IDR cost currency, no mineral royalty schedule (the 1.5% trademark fee sits inside opex), house rf/crp and terminal g are read consistently with the macro deck. The peer set is the engine's INDUSTRIAL_GOODS default and includes IMPC and SCCO, which is noted but not decisive because ARNA drives the medians.

conservatism_audit.note: Below last actual with no dispositive source: gross margin capped at 25.5% in perpetuity, 1.3pp under the FY2022-25 average and 1.3pp under FY2025, although Q3 2026 gross margin already recovered to 23.2%; terminal g 4.0% versus c.8.6% nominal GDP; a 20% liquidity discount asserted as house without a cited rule; and a 5.6% yield that understates the 9.9% TTM. The bear/bull shocks themselves are properly mirrored.

calibration.note: Both BLOCK flags are substantively justified: the -6.0pp FY2026E margin gap is the actual 9M run-rate, and the +3.4pp gross-margin drift is a sourced cycle recovery. But FY2026E cash of 387.7 and net debt of -183.1 do not reconcile to the 30 Sep actuals of 266.1 and -33.9, implying an undisclosed c.100bn Q4 working-capital release.

signoff.notes: The trough-year base is the nine-month actual (revenue -7.4%, gross margin 22.1%, capex 5.46% of sales, working capital 51.5%) and the recovery to the FY2022-25 margin average by FY2030E is sourced to the property cycle, not assumed. The 20% liquidity discount is mechanical from the turnover band and stated as such, the unfunded Rp384.7bn employee-benefit liability is now charged in full, the associates are marked at 12x earnings rather than book, and the earnings cross-checks are stated on FY2025A rather than trough earnings. C1-C13 answered on substance. The multiple and P/B-ROE cross-checks bracket the DCF. Approve.

bias.note: FY2026E is set to the 9M actuals (revenue 1,605.0 against 1,817.5, gross margin 21.8%, opex 11.0%); terminal gross margin 25.8% is the FY2022-25 average and not the 26.8% peak; opex never returns to the FY2025 9.5% and terminal growth of 4.5% sits under the 5% cap, so the drivers are anchored or conservative. Offsetting optimism: the revenue path passes the FY2025 peak in FY2028 although the text says not before FY2030; FY2026E revenue is set 1.9% above a nine-month run-rate on an unreproducible Q4 leg; and the FY2026E dividend cash outflow omits the December interim. The two directions roughly cancel and neither tail has a sourced driver.

recomputed.item: Net debt at 30 Sep 2026 (cash 266.07 less bank debt 83.58 less leases 148.55)
Share of FY2025 profit of associates (SGP 50pct x 48.55, SPN 49pct x 14.13)

findings.finding: The investment summary states the bridge net position as net cash of -202.6, the FY2025A net debt, while the valuation bridge uses the 30 September 2026 net debt of -33.9 before the Rp148.5bn lease add-back (adjusted net cash Rp182.4bn). The gap is Rp168.7bn, Rp16.3 a share, 5.9% of the target. The judge raised the same point.

FY2026E dividends_paid is Rp134.16bn, i.e. Rp13.0 a share at the model FY2025A dps line, which is the June 2026 final alone (consistent with the C5 answer and S2). The FY2025 declared total was Rp23.0 (engine dps_ttm 23) and section 7 says a December interim has been paid in each of the last five years; section 3 says the fourth quarter pays the December interim dividend, but no such payment is in the model. Closing cash of Rp302.7bn and net cash of -70.6 are therefore overstated by roughly Rp103bn and the year closes at about net debt Rp33bn, not net cash. The valuation does not use this line, but section 3 calls the reconciliation deliberately tight.

The div_yield method (Rp194, -46.5% against the DCF, weight 10%) capitalises the FY2026E trough DPS of Rp14 at the 7.22% peer yield, while both earnings cross-checks are deliberately anchored to FY2025A to avoid counting the cycle twice. On the Rp23 declared for FY2025 the same method gives Rp319, above the DCF rather than 47% below it. The section 4 trough-year floor reading does not hold: a trough distribution capitalised at a peer yield is a trough value, not a floor.

Section 4 does not reproduce the engine COE of 11.59%: rf 7.4% plus mature ERP 4.2% plus CRP 2.5% at a 0.86 levered beta is 13.2% (14.1% unlevered). The engine applies the CRP at a reduced weight (crp 0.0246, coe 0.11587, de 0.097, kd 0.0945, wacc 0.1121). Separately the cost_of_debt input is 8.1% (FY2025 finance cost 16.6 on opening debt 204.6) while section 4 states 9.4% and calls it consistent with those same figures; 9.4% is what the engine uses.

The FY2026E gross margin of 22.1% is described in the input basis, in the drift justification and in section 3 as the nine-month actual. F26/F24 give 349.73/1,605.01 = 21.8%; the 4.3pp fall against 9M2025 is right but the level is not. The modelled year sits 0.3pp above its own stated anchor.

Section 3 says neither segment is assumed to recover its FY2025 peak before the end of the decade and the revenue basis says the base does not assume a return to the FY2025 sales peak before FY2030, but FY2028E revenue of Rp2,415.0bn is already 2.6% above FY2025A of Rp2,354.4bn and FY2030E is 12.6% above it. The report claims a conservatism the model does not deliver.

The summary says the associates earned only 759.4 of net assets into a low single-digit return. Rp759.4bn is the SPN equity alone (F53); the pair combined equity is Rp1,492.6bn (SGP 733.1 plus SPN 759.4) and 4.2% is the blended return, which is the number the 12x mark is argued from.

The bear narrative (property completions depressed through 2027, gross margin near the 2026 trough, section 5 another leg down) is not what the mirrored shocks do: revenue growth is only 3pp lower, so FY2027E still grows 2.0%, and the margin path still reaches 24.3% permanently, above the 22.1% trough. Bull +19.3% against bear -13.7% on the same shocks also lifts the probability-weighted value above the base. Align the narrative with the shocks so the bear is not read as deeper than it is.
Section 4 says the P/B-ROE results bracket our DCF. They do not: the FY2025A 14.0% ROE gives about Rp333 and FY2027E 9.1% about Rp176, bracketing the Rp319 method blend, both below the Rp362 DCF.

Expected return of 25.6% sits 0.6pp above the 25.0% BUY threshold in fund record; a 1-2% move in any one driver flips the rating to ADD. The DCF haircut for the exit-multiple expansion is named as the weak link but not quantified.

The FY2026E revenue basis (a Q4 at the Q3 run-rate) implies Q4 2026 revenue of Rp575.1bn, +7.1 pct against Q4 2025, with no standalone Q3 revenue in the facts to reproduce it. The compounder output contract is also incomplete: no reinvestment rate times ROIIC, no named fade mechanism (ROE 14.0% to 12.0% by FY2035E is implied but not argued) and no owner-earnings bridge from reported net income.
